text:
Sam: heads-up — noticed a correlated rise in per-token P50 on route /generate-chat from pool 'eu-west-3-dedicated-42' starting ~17:10 UTC, concurrent with CPU jitter on node g2-11
Maya: can you paste the quick query? I want to see KV cache hit rates around that time
Sam: digging, but initial look: KV hit dropped from 92% -> 60% for long-context workloads, batching latency up ~45ms. here's the log snippet I grabbed:
```
Sam@perf-agent: 2026-04-02T17:09:57Z pool=eu-west-3-dedicated-42 node=g2-11 kernel=matmul_fast batch_size=4 kv_hit=false token_lat=78ms
Sam@perf-agent: 2026-04-02T17:10:12Z pool=eu-west-3-dedicated-42 node=g2-11 kernel=matmul_fast batch_size=8 kv_hit=false token_lat=123ms
```
Ashley: ugh that looks like a KV eviction storm + increased batching causing CPU thrash. Any noisy neighbor signals from the infra side?
Dan: infra shows a burst of compiler jobs on the same host (OOM killer not triggered). I flagged it as noisy-neighbor in the infra dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dash/pools/42/nbr. perf-bot also emitted a high-contention alert at 17:08
perf-bot: ALERT: pool-saturation-high (pool=eu-west-3-dedicated-42) severity=warning agents=3
Maya: we need better instrumentation in the per-pool dashboard: token-level breakdown (KV hit vs miss), kernel path used, per-node batching distribution, and a headroom metric that decays slowly to show sustained pressure
Sam: agreed. Proposed minimal metric additions for the dashboard panels:
- token.kv_hit_rate (by route, by pool)
- token.kernel_selector (hot counts per kernel)
- token.per_token_latency.p50/p95 (split by kv_hit=true/false)
- pool.headroom_estimate (capacity left in tokens/s considering current batching)
Maya: also add a noisy_neigh_score = (cpu_jitter_pct * (1 - kv_hit_rate)) + compile_job_rate*0.5 so we can surface suspects automatically
Ashley: can we compute kernel selector attribution without changing runtime? maybe sample a small % of requests with selector_debug=true and emit kernel_id tag
Dan: yes, config flag in runtime already exists: selector.debug_sample_rate. set to 0.5% for next 8 hours and route to a low-cost trace sink. I can toggle from infra side.
Sam: rollout plan:
1) enable selector.debug_sample_rate=0.5% in pool 42 (Dan)
2) add token.kv_hit_rate and per_token_latency split to eng-platform metrics (Maya + Ashley)
3) wire noisy_neigh_score and headroom_estimate into pool overview and alerting (on call)
4) run 6h synthetic traffic and compare pre/post dashboard graphs
Maya: will create a PR for the dashboard JSON and alert rules, tagging @Ashley and @Dan. summary will include query examples and a small viz for KV hit split.
Ashley: quick queries to include in the PR:
```
# KV hit rate by route
sum(rate(token_count{pool="eu-west-3-dedicated-42",kv_hit="true"}[5m])) / sum(rate(token_count{pool="eu-west-3-dedicated-42"}[5m]))

# per-token p95 where kv_miss
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_duration_seconds_bucket{kv_hit="false",pool="eu-west-3-dedicated-42"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Dan: will flip the sample flag and keep an eye. If noisy_neigh_score > 0.6 for >10m, auto-create an incident draft in /incidents and ping infra-oncall
Sam: thanks. can someone own the baseline capture for the synthetic run? want to compare kernel mix and batching distribution pre/post
Maya: I’ll run the synthetic harness against pool 42 at 02:00 UTC tomorrow, capture kernel IDs, batch_size histogram, kv_hit flags, and token lat percentiles. will attach results to the dashboard PR
Ashley: nit — add an extra panel showing 'route-concurrency vs per-token latency' scatter so product teams can see route-specific SLO impact
Sam: perfect. leaving action items -> Maya (dashboard + synthetic), Dan (enable sample, monitor), Ashley (metrics instrument + PR tweaks). I’ll follow up after the 6h run. :thumbsup:
Dan: noted, toggling selector sampling now. will post a short update in this thread when it's live
perf-bot: ACTION_LOG: selector.debug_sample_rate set to 0.5% for pool eu-west-3-dedicated-42 by Dan at 2026-04-02T17:23:10Z
